doc.title: Konitz Lee — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: The Tristano group and leaving for Kenton
title: First recording with Tristano and writing 'Subconscious-Lee'
summary: He explains why the New Jazz date came to him via Tony Fruscella, and that 'Subconscious-Lee' and 'Tautology' began as lesson exercises.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Okay. While you’re playing with Miles’ nonet you were also rehearsing with Tristano?

And beginning in nineteen forty-nine you started recording with him. The first record date is for what was then called “New Jazz” which became “Prestige”. I read that you were originally offered the date with Tony Fruscella. Can you talk about that?

He came by my apartment at that time to talk it over and try some things. I made some suggestions that apparently offended him, I can’t say exactly what it was, but it must have been with the selection of material that I didn’t know and wasn’t ready to play. He backed out and I suggested getting Lennie and Shelly Manne, and Arnold Fishkin . . . and Billy Bauer. I don’t know that Warne was around then.
For that one you had written maybe the most famous of all, certainly your tunes and maybe of all the tunes written by anybody in the Tristano school,”Subconcious-Lee”.
I still get royalties from that little exercise I did for my lesson.
So that’s what it was? An exercise?

Yeah. He said to write out a solo piece and that’s what I enjoy doing and I still do that. I never carried it over into orchestration, per se, and pop tunes. These are more like “embellishment” kinds of things.
How about “Tautology” which also you recorded later that year?
They were all kind of that idea. When I realized that they were playable I had that in mind certainly.
